title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Several templating anions, including mixed anion sets, locally organize recognizable smaller hydroxide units and sit in cages or cavities of the finished cluster, so the anion combination changes the assembled architecture.
explanation: Cl− with NO3− templates sandwich wheels of vertex-sharing [Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)]9+ and cubane-like [Gd3Ni(μ3-OH)4]7+ units (Gd36Ni12) and related tubes (Gd48, Er48). ClO4− with CO32− gives bowl-like Ln42M10 and cagelike Gd27 built from cubane and larger hydroxide fragments, with perchlorate in the cavities. Encapsulated perchlorates in Dy24Mn2 are held by hydrogen bonding.
scope: High-nuclearity lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters whose cores are formally assemblies of cubanes, square pyramids, or related small hydroxide units.
conditions: Mixed or multiple small anions (Cl−/NO3−, ClO4−/CO32−, or several ClO4−) present during assembly and located crystallographically inside the core.
caveats: Functions (charge balance, geometry, fragment templating) are assigned from crystal structures. Markdown formulas for several of these clusters are corrupted, so exact stoichiometries should be checked against the cited papers.
